Row.Text: Two chiefs, flanked by their warriors, enter the council house as the Shawnee delegation looks on. Under Shawnee eyes, grievances are aired in tones tense but measured. The Shawnee diplomat makes a proposition: unite, there are greater threats than one’s neighbor.
Such efforts would be much improved with a division of diplomats.
Shawnee diplomats can offer advice, but nothing more.

A prominent Shawnee diplomat proposes an assembly: lesser states can meet and air grievances under Shawnee protection, without the interference of major powers. Shawnee economists see this as an opportunity for a trade league, even, a Shawnee Stock Exchange.
What is sensible diplomacy rarely follows economic gain.
What is sensible diplomacy always follows economic gain.
